evidence:
Statement location: sections/appendix.tex line 285 ("Where the approach does not apply"). refs.bib has no Srebro, Gunasekar or Ongie entries.

(1) Srebro, Rennie, Jaakkola, "Maximum-Margin Matrix Factorization", NIPS 17 (2004). Confirmed on the NeurIPS proceedings page. I read the PDF directly; its Lemma 1 states: ||X||_Sigma = min_{X=UV'} ||U||_Fro ||V||_Fro = min_{X=UV'} 1/2(||U||_Fro^2+||V||_Fro^2). This is the pricing fact: L2 weight decay on a two-factor linear product equals the trace (nuclear) norm.

(2) Ongie, Willett, "The Role of Linear Layers in Nonlinear Interpolating Networks", arXiv 2202.00856 (2022). This is the closest match to our setting.
- Intro: "adding linear layers to a ReLU network with weight decay regularization is akin to using a two-layer ReLU network with nuclear or Schatten norm regularization on the weight matrix."
- Lemma 3.2: R_L(f) = min (1/L)||a||^2 + ((L-1)/L)||W||_{S_q}^q with q = 2/(L-1). A single linear layer (L=3) gives q=1, the nuclear norm (Sec. 3 before Lemma 3.8: "the Phi_3 loss involves minimizing over the nuclear norm of a matrix").
- Published venue unconfirmed: dblp and Semantic Scholar were blocked or rate-limited, and the WebSearch budget was used up.

(3) Gunasekar et al., "Implicit Regularization in Matrix Factorization", NIPS 30 (2017). Confirmed on the proceedings page. It shows an implicit gradient-descent bias toward the minimum nuclear norm. That is about gradient descent, not an explicit L2 price, so it is optional.

Caveat: the clause "rewards carrying many frequencies in one neuron" is the paper's own reading, and none of these sources states it. Cite them for the nuclear-norm pricing only.

recommended_citations.why: Supports 'priced by a nuclear norm'. Lemma 1: the trace norm equals the minimum over factorizations X=UV' of 1/2(||U||_F^2+||V||_F^2), i.e. L2 weight decay on a product of linear factors.

Supports the whole sentence in the network setting. Lemma 3.2: adding linear layers in front of ReLU neurons under weight decay gives a Schatten-q price (q=2/(L-1)) on the inner weight matrix; one linear layer gives the nuclear norm. Title, authors and year confirmed; published venue not confirmed, so cited as arXiv.
Optional, tangential. Shows gradient descent on a factorisation is implicitly biased toward the minimum nuclear norm. Use only if the sentence should also mention training dynamics.

recommended_change: In appendix.tex l.285, change "the shared layer is priced by a nuclear norm" to "the shared layer is priced by a nuclear norm \citep{srebro2004mmmf,ongie2022linear}". Keep "that rewards carrying many frequencies in one neuron" as our own gloss; do not attribute it to the citations. Add the srebro2004mmmf and ongie2022linear bib entries. Gunasekar 2017 is optional.
